name: Juggernaut Method

lead: The Juggernaut Method is a strength training template built around waves of loading, with weeks that vary rep targets and intensity across a training block. It comes from Chad Wesley Smith's Juggernaut Training Systems.

For looks, the chain is simple: progressive strength work on the big lifts supports more muscle and a more developed physique. Lifters on strength forums describe it alongside 5/3/1 and conjugate approaches, and as a way to push heavier weights; there are no controlled studies of the method itself.

paras: Lifters follow it from the book or spreadsheet, or through the JuggernautAI app, which logs sessions. Forum logs show people running parts of it, such as only the heavier waves, and combining it with accessory work or conjugate blocks.
Risks are those of heavy lifting in general: overreaching, fatigue and injury if load and recovery are mismanaged. Forum users describe fatigue and adjusting the program.

angle.text: The template organises heavy lifting into repeating waves so that strength builds over weeks, which lifters link to a bigger, stronger-looking body.

lead: The Juggernaut Method is a wave-loading strength template from Juggernaut Training Systems, used by lifters on forums such as T Nation as an alternative to programs like 5/3/1, Westside conjugate and the Texas Method [1].

People use it to get stronger on the main barbell lifts, which they connect to building muscle and a more developed physique. Users report running full cycles, the heavier 5 and 3 waves only for a focus on heavy weight, or an inverse version [1][2].
A related product, JuggernautAI, is an app that generates and logs training; forum logs show people recording its sessions [3].

paras: The method organises training into waves in which rep targets and intensity change from week to week. Forum users refer to running only the 5 and 3 waves to emphasise heavy weights [1], and to an inverse variant [2]. Details of the program are given in its book and spreadsheet [2].

On T Nation, the method is named alongside 5/3/1, Dan John's one-lift-a-day approach and linear periodisation when members discuss weekly changes in load [4]. One user eased back into conjugate training with four to five weeks of Juggernaut before two weeks of maximal-effort work [5]. Others log JuggernautAI sessions with squats, deadlifts and accessory supersets [3].
